Blocking architecture finding: this implementation uses deterministic substring/path predicates as the semantic decision procedure for amendment grounds. Those checks can validate evidence addresses, but they do not establish `UNSATISFIABLE_AT_BASE`, `MUTUALLY_UNSATISFIABLE`, or `REQUIRES_BREAKING_HOUSE_RULE`. KOD-97 explicitly describes a fresh reconciler/refuter session. Preserve deterministic evidence collection and ordered writes, but move semantic judgment behind a typed structured-output reconciler boundary. Canonical issue finding: KOD-97 comment `2468abe7-75f5-48df-877c-f6113f61cc33`.

commits.messageBody:
Each ground is its own claim model and asks the repository at the resolved
base its own question: an address the tree does not carry, a carried file
without the quoted premise, an anchor really present that two criteria
demand differently, a rule really written in the repository's own rules
document. No single reading answers two of them, so relabelling carries no
evidence across — the models will not even accept each other's fields.

Eight fixtures pair every ground both ways over one two-commit repository,
whose second commit moves every fact the four grounds read; a matrix holds
the label constant and lets the base move the arm in opposite directions.

commits.messageBody:
… (KOD-653)

A claim the base does not bear out, a subject the issue does not hold as a
criterion, and an address the base cannot read as one regular file all land
in the same arm: UPHELD, named against the criterion it refused. A refusal
writes nothing, and the identical reconciler rewrites exactly one body when
the ground is proved, so the byte-identity assertion has something to fail
against. The base ref is the run's, not the claimant's — failing to resolve
it stays an error rather than becoming a verdict about the criterion.
